_comment: CANONICAL-WINNER ENFORCE set. A CLOSED, curated list of DISTINCT model families that must WIN over a disagreeing raw_family when the model ID itself names the family (the ID-derived family equals one of these). This covers BOTH (a) the own-family-enforce ledger (a provider mislabels a distinct model as its parent: aion/magnum as 'llama', mixtral/pixtral/voxtral as 'mistral', wizardlm/inflection as 'gpt', intellect as 'glm', qwq as 'qwen', weaver as 'alpha') AND (b) the vendor/org-namespace leak (raw_family is the ID's ORG, not a family: nousresearch->hermes, allenai->olmo, liquid->lfm). In reconcileIDDriven, when the ID-driven family differs from raw_family AND the ID-driven family is in this set, the ID-driven decomposition (family+variant+version+modifier) is adopted wholesale — the raw mislabel/org is discarded. The set is closed (no per-name runtime guessing): only an ID whose own leading token resolves to one of these distinct families triggers the override. Sorted alphabetically. The 2026-08-28 catalog refresh RETIRED two entries: upstream dropped every codellama row and every owl row, so both became dead/speculative curation (TestFamilyEnforce_IntegrityGuard requires every entry to ground in >=1 vendored-catalog model) and were removed. Re-add either the moment upstream serves it again. 'meta' is handled separately via family_aliases (meta->llama), not here. inkling and kling are one three-way collision of class (a): the vendored catalog ships raw_family "ling" verbatim on ALL 14 rows -- Thinking Machines' 6 Inkling rows AND the 8 klingai/kling-v* video rows -- so both were folded onto inclusionAI's unrelated Ling family. The IDs themselves are correct and always were (vercel spells its rows klingai/kling-v2.5-turbo-i2v, leading 'k' intact), so the ID-driven decomposition is authoritative and the two ledger rows split all 14 without a single exact-ID pin.
